sentences.text: The petitioner is the accused in C.C.No. 1305/2019 on the file of the Court of the Judicial First Class Magistrate, Chalakkudy and in C.C.No.176 of 2020 on the file of the Court of the Judicial First Class Magistrate-I, Koundungallur ('Trial Courts', for short), for allegedly committing the offence punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code.

sentences.text: 2. The petitioner has stated in the Criminal Miscellaneous Case that, he is totally innocent of the allegations levelled against him.
The petitioner was totally unaware of the above cases.
It is only when he went to renew his passport, he learnt regarding the plendency of the cases.

Even though he is ready and willing to return to India and get himself enlarged on bail, he is unable to come down,
because the validity of his passport has expired.

Likewise, he is also apprehensive that, if he comes down to India, he may be CRL.MC NO.2499 of 2026 4 2026:KER:27790 arrested at the Airport and his applications for bail may not be considered on the date of surrender.

Hence, the Crl.M.C.
3.
I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.

Sanju vs State Of Kerala on 27 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77361729/
2 4.

On a consideration of the facts and materials on record, I dispose of the Crl.M.C. in the following manner:
(i) It would be upto the petitioner to approach the fifth respondent and file an application for issuance of an emergency certificate.
If an application for an emergency certificate is filed within two weeks from today, the fifth respondent shall consider the application, in accordance with law, and as expeditiously as possible.
(ii) The petitioner shall return to India within a week from the date of receipt of the emergency certificate.
(iii) On arriving in India, the petitioner is directed to report before the Investigating Officer in Crime No.369/2019 of the Vellikulangara Police Station, Thrissur.

(iv) The Investigating Officer is directed to obtain the phone number, address and the other details of the petitioner, and ensure that he surrenders before the Trial Courts within a week from the date of his arrival in India.
However, the Investigating Officer shall not enforce the NBW.

(v) On the petitioner surrendering before the Trial Courts, and filing applications to recall the NBW and to enlarge him on bail, the Trial Courts shall consider the applications, in accordance with law,
on the day that the petitioner surrenders before the Trial Court.

(vi) In order to enable the petitioner to surrender before the Trial Courts, the NBW issued against the petitioner shall be kept in abeyance for one week from the day he arrives in India, provided the petitioner appears before the Investigating Officer on the day he returns to India, and surrenders before the Trial Courts within a week thereafter.
